The Buckeyes will look to keep that momentum rolling Saturday, but a surging Iowa team and a trip to Kinnick Stadium present a potential trap-game scenario.

It's a trap game that Jeremiah Smith , Julian Sayin and No. 6 Ohio State will look to avoid at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 3 when the Buckeyes go toe-to-toe with No. 14 Iowa inside Kinnick Stadium for 60 minutes in the Big Ten-ranked matchup of the week.

The Hawkeyes earned the right to host ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday in Iowa City, Iowa thanks to Hank Brown's game-winning touchdown last week on the road in Ann Arbor against Michigan. Iowa's 20-19 win over Michigan marked the Hawkeyes first ranked Big Ten road win since 2021.

Iowa will have its hands full on Saturday as it defends Smith, who is on the verge of breaking multiple records for Ohio State receivers. The Heisman Trophy betting favorite finished with 12 receptions for 217 receiving yards and four touchdowns last week against Illinois.

articles.title: El Almería remonta para seguir con el pleno de victorias en casa
articles.standfirst: Cipenga y Miguel de la Fuente voltearon el tanto inicial de Karrikaburu para doblegar a un Burgos combativo
articles.summary: Cipenga y Miguel de la Fuente voltearon el tanto inicial de Karrikaburu para doblegar a un Burgos combativo
articles.body: El Almería firmó una remontada de carácter para derrotar al Burgos (2-1) y enlazar su quinta victoria consecutiva. Los rojiblancos se vieron por detrás en el marcador tras el tanto de Karrikaburu antes del descanso, pero reaccionaron en la segunda mitad con los goles de Cipenga y Miguel de la Fuente para culminar la primera remontada liguera de la era García Pimienta y mantener su excelente momento de forma. Los almerienses comenzaron el encuentro llevando el peso del juego, aunque sin encontrar el camino hacia la portería rival. García Pimienta se encontró con el primer contratiempo a los 18 minutos, cuando se vio obligado a retirar a Vesga, lesionado tras un golpe en el tobillo derecho, para dar entrada a Quim. La ocasión más clara de los rojiblancos llegó en el minuto 36, cuando Cipenga firmó una magnífica acción individual para plantarse solo ante Cantero. Sin embargo, su remate, demasiado defectuoso, desperdició una oportunidad inmejorable. El fútbol, una vez más, castigó la falta de acierto local. En la primera llegada con verdadero peligro del Burgos, apenas cuatro minutos después, Karrikaburu firmó el 0-1 antes del descanso con un remate de primeras en el área pequeña tras un preciso centro raso de Llabrés. Thalys, con un remate de cabeza que se marchó desviado cerca de la portería rival, y Baptistao, que estuvo a punto de embocar a gol un disparo forzado en el segundo palo, estuvieron cerca de poner las tablas antes del paso por vestuarios. La segunda mitad arrancó sin cambios y con un Almería decidido a darle la vuelta al marcador. En el minuto 56, Arribas filtró un pase magnífico para Quim dentro del área, pero el centrocampista apenas pudo imprimirle fuerza a un disparo que ejecutó mientras perdía el equilibrio. Poco después, el propio Arribas lo intentó desde la frontal con un remate que se marchó rozando el larguero, antes de que Cantero firmara, a la hora de juego, una intervención espectacular para desviar un potente cabezazo de Bonini y evitar el empate. Los rojiblancos continuaron acumulando ocasiones. Miguel de la Fuente dispuso de otra clarísima, pero, con todo a favor, sólo alcanzó a rozar el balón en el área pequeña. Tanto insistió el Almería que acabó encontrando el premio. En el minuto 77, Cipenga igualó el encuentro con un certero remate de cabeza en el segundo palo tras un magnífico centro con rosca de Arribas. La remontada se consumó siete minutos después con un auténtico golazo de Miguel de la Fuente. El delantero se resarció de su ocasión fallada al sacar un potente disparo seco desde la media luna que se coló junto a la base del poste de la portería defendida por Cantero. Un 2-1 definitivo que desató la euforia en el UD Almería Stadium y certificó la quinta victoria consecutiva del conjunto de García Pimienta.

articles.title: How Barcelona star was central to Spain’s press this international break
articles.summary: Barcelona star Pedri is one of the best midfielders in the world, and he is coming off a World Cup triumph with Spain in the summer.The Canary Islander might...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Pedri is one of the best midfielders in the world, and he is coming off a World Cup triumph with Spain in the summer.

The Canary Islander might not have been a guaranteed starter for La Roja at the tournament in North America, but he still managed to leave a mark.

His ability on the ball has never been difficult to appreciate, but FIFA's technical analysis of the 2026 World Cup has highlighted a less celebrated part of the Barcelona midfielder's game.

According to Diario SPORT , FIFA's technical study placed Pedri at the top of the tournament for involvement in counter-pressing actions.

It offers another indication that the 23-year-old's influence extends well beyond controlling possession and creating chances.

Spain activated their counter-press in 60.1% of eligible situations in the opposition half, the highest percentage at the World Cup.

They recovered possession 39 times through those situations, nine more than France. Almost half of those recoveries, 48%, arrived within one to three seconds of losing the ball.

Pedri was not a guaranteed starter for Spain at the World Cup. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Pedri was central to making that system work. His intelligence allowed him to think beyond the next pass.

The midfielder positioned himself to receive and progress possession, aspects that often go unnoticed in the larger context of the game.

Barcelona fingerprints all over Spain's success

Pedri was not the only Barça player prominent in FIFA's analysis.

Dani Olmo ranked seventh for counter-pressing actions per 30 minutes without possession, while Rodri produced a tournament-leading seven recoveries from the mechanism.

Pau Cubarsi added five such recoveries, the joint-third-highest total at the tournament. Those numbers help explain why Spain's defensive performance was so impressive.

They conceded only once and allowed just 0.31 expected goals per match, the competition's lowest figure.

There is an obvious connection to be made with Hansi Flick's Barcelona.

Barça want to dominate possession, but maintaining that dominance requires an immediate reaction when the ball is lost.

Pedri embodies exactly what Hansi Flick wants from his team. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The best possession teams do not simply keep the ball exceptionally well. They make opponents feel as though they cannot keep it either.

Pedri is fundamental to both sides of that coin. His passing and press resistance make Barça better when they have possession.

His anticipation and positioning help them recover it when they do not. The Spaniard might not have had a lights-out World Cup, but he has returned to his best since the start of the season.

It is good to see such numbers underline Pedri's unique quality, and it remains to be seen how he fares for the rest of the campaign and beyond.

articles.title: Gillingham 0-0 Newport
articles.summary: Gillingham and Newport battled to a dour 0-0 draw at Priestfield in League Two.
articles.body:
The Gills had most of the ball, but it was the Exiles who had more opportunities to snatch three points.

County looked dangerous early on and were only denied a lead inside the opening 10 minutes when James Brophy blocked Michael Adu-Poku's shot on the line.

Home goalkeeper Ollie Wright was then called into action to keep out Harrison Biggins' free-kick.

Adu-Poku was kept out by Wright on the half-hour mark before Matty Jacob squandered the best chance of the first period when he fired the rebound into the side netting.

Newport soon went close again when Christian Doidge hit the crossbar following a Biggins free-kick.

After the break, Brophy fired an effort wide of the mark as the Gills struggled to create big chances.

With 10 minutes to go Biggins struck a free-kick over the bar before Wright proved his worth once again late on with a super stop to deny County defender Cameron Norman.

Gills could have won it in stoppage time but Bradley Dack nodded just over the bar.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Salford 1-0 Fleetwood
articles.summary: Macaulay Langstaff scored as in-form Salford battled to a 1-0 win over Fleetwood to move top of League Two.
articles.body:
Salford, who won four of their five league matches in September, missed a golden chance to take the lead in the seventh minute when Langstaff burst into the box and fired wide.

Will Norris made a superb diving save to touch Adam Murphy's effort onto the post before Mark Helm skewed a shot over the bar from range as the visitors threatened to open the scoring 10 minutes later.

Former Fleetwood forward Ryan Graydon had a shot blocked inside the box as the first half petered out after its lively start.

The Cod Army were given a lifeline 13 minutes after the break when it was judged the ball had gone behind for a goal kick before Kelly Nmai's low centre ricocheted into the visitors' net.

But Fleetwood's reprieve was to be short-lived as Salford went ahead after 65 minutes when Langstaff diverted Graydon's effort from range into the top right corner.

Away goalkeeper Jay Lynch made two fine saves to deny Jorge Grant's curling shot from the edge of the box and a fierce Graydon drive as the Ammies comfortably held on.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Crewe 3-1 Bristol Rovers
articles.summary: A first-half double from Jack Lankester helped unbeaten Crewe to an emphatic 3-1 win over fellow high-fliers Bristol Rovers.
articles.body:
Jordan Gibson added a third after the break as Rovers - with boss Steve Evans watching from the stand as he served a touchline ban - sunk to a fourth away defeat in five games, with Bobby Kamwa's brilliant late strike scant consolation.

Lankester got Crewe off to a thrilling start with a goal after just 40 seconds. He latched onto a ball from Joel Tabiner, cut in from the right flank and curled an exquisite effort into the far corner past goalkeeper Brad Young.

Rovers responded quickly and as the ball bounced around the home box, Ciaran Kelly unleashed a shot onto the underside of the crossbar.

After curling a free-kick just over, Lankester punished the visitors, sending Young the wrong way from the penalty spot after Alfie Kilgour was spotted pulling down Luke Offord at a corner.

It could have got worse for Rovers shortly afterwards as Adrien Thibaut raced clear and it needed a last-ditch intervention from Jack Sparkes to block the young striker's effort.

Rovers improved after the break and Kamwa was slipped clear only to be denied by Crewe goalkeeper Tom Booth.

But the contest was put out of their reach in the 66th minute. Josh March swept a pass over to the right of the box where substitute Gibson brought the ball down and drilled a fine finish into the far corner.

Kamwa grabbed a sensational goal in stoppage time when he spotted Booth off his line and drove the ball over him from inside his own half.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Leyton Orient 0-2 Plymouth
articles.summary: Plymouth went top of League One after two goals in five minutes gave them a 2-0 win at Leyton Orient.
articles.body:
Efforts by Bim Pepple and Will Evans produced Argyle's response to defeat by Burton last week.

Fin Stevens shot wide of the upright after just three minutes for Orient, while Oliver Irow forced Nathan Baxter to stretch out and palm his effort away at the other end.

However, the rest of the half was a scrappy affair.

The damage caused by Plymouth came in six minutes after the restart.

Firstly, a scramble following a corner in the 52nd minute fell to Bradley Ibrahim who put the ball across goal for Pepple to poke home his fifth league goal of the campaign.

Soon after, a deep cross by Ronan Curtis from the right found the head of Evans who directed it into the net for his third of the season.

Stevens volleyed at Argyle goalkeeper Murphy Cooper in the 68th minute as Orient pushed for a way back, but they could not prevent Plymouth going top.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Grimsby 1-2 Shrewsbury
articles.summary: Shrewsbury claimed a priceless first away victory of the Sky Bet League Two campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 triumph over Grimsby at Blundell Park.
articles.body:
George Lloyd gave Salop a one-goal lead going into the break before Kian McMahon-Brown doubled their advantage on the hour mark, with Finlay Cartwright's first Mariners goal being only a consolation.

Will Brook was forced into a save early on as Charles Vernam ran through on goal, with Harvey Rodgers unable to make use of the rebound.

Shrewsbury took the lead in the 19th minute through former Grimsby loanee Lloyd, who got the final touch as the ball was headed into his path from a corner.

The visitors doubled their lead on the hour when McMahon-Brown struck a well-controlled volley into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Justin Amaluzor had a close-range effort blocked well from a long throw, and Edon Pruti shot just wide from a cutback, but it was substitute Cartwright who headed Grimsby's reply in the 75th minute, provided by another replacement - Iwan Morgan.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Burton 1-3 Huddersfield
articles.summary: Huddersfield handed Burton their first home league defeat of the season with a 3-1 victory at the Pirelli Stadium.
articles.body:
Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored one and set up another in a dominant first half for Town, with Finn Delap lashing home his third goal of the season to briefly have Albion level.

The Terriers started the stronger and deservedly took the lead after 22 minutes, Fernandes seizing on a poor pass from Delap across his own penalty area and instinctively firing home.

Burton struggled to threaten their opponents in the first half-hour but were level when Caylan Vickers teed up Delap and the young defender atoned for his earlier error with a fearsome rising drive beyond Matt Young into the top corner.

Town scored a second before the break and this time Fernandes was the provider with a right-wing cross, which Bali Mumba, ghosting into space in the area, finished from five yards.

Delap was close to his second of the game with another fierce shot early in the second half, but this time Young made a good save to deny him.

Instead Huddersfield were gifted a third goal with minutes remaining, George Evans putting his own keeper under pressure with a loose back pass and Ashley Fletcher nipping in to score from close range.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Exeter 1-0 Rotherham
articles.summary: Anthony Scully marked his Exeter debut with the only goal of the game in a 1-0 League Two win over Rotherham at St James Park.
articles.body:
The winger, whose Dad Tony had a productive 13-match loan spell with the Grecians in 2005, was only announced as a new signing of the morning of the game but settled a contest Exeter dominated shortly after half-time.

Exeter started well with Scully seeing a goal-bound shot blocked by Dom Iorfa, while Rotherham went close when Marvin Kaleta broke free down the right but his low cross was just too far in front of Paul Mullin.

Scully then put Taylor Perry through on goal but he lifted his shot over Rotherham goalkeeper Julian Eyestone and wide.

The deadlock was broken on 51 minutes after superb work by Charlie Cummins set George Birch free and his cross was turned in from close range by Scully.

Exeter continued to dominate with Josh Gordon's header saved by Eyestone, while Ethan Sutherland smashed a volley against the outside of the post with his first contribution after coming off the bench.

Rotherham had a chance deep into stoppage time to rescue a point but Mullin scuffed his shot wide of the near post.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Accrington 2-0 Cheltenham
articles.summary: Cheltenham squandered the chance to go top of Sky Bet League Two as Charlie Warren scored a late double in a 2-0 win for Accrington.
articles.body:
On-loan Bolton striker Warren struck in the 78th and 87th minutes to inflict only a second league defeat of the season on the Robins, who had Charlie McCann sent off for a second yellow card in added time.

In the first half, Devon Matthews volleyed over while Alex Henderson's strike was tipped away by goalkeeper Wyll Stanway.

The Cheltenham keeper kept out a Stefan Mols effort with his foot and also pushed away a Joe Anderson strike before the break.

Stanley continued to press, with Josh Woods firing over from six yards in the 63rd minute before another Woods strike took a deflection to take the ball narrowly wide.

Stanley found a way through after 78 minutes when Connor O'Brien's deep cross found substitute Warren who controlled the ball and fired home.

It was his first League Two goal and his second came shortly afterwards. A Mols corner was not cleared and Warren pounced to make the three points safe as Town ended the game with 10 men.

What the result means and next fixtures...
